methods.label: Identify the diameter
methods.explanation: The chord subtending the right angle is a diameter, so the hypotenuse is the diameter of the circumcircle, and its center is the midpoint of the hypotenuse.
methods.levelReason: Uses the Grade 9 converse of the diameter-angle theorem and the definition of a diameter.

methods.label: Find a point equally far from the vertices
methods.explanation:
Let \(\triangle ABC\) have its right angle at \(A\), and let \(M\) be the midpoint of hypotenuse \(BC\). The median-to-the-hypotenuse theorem gives
\[
AM=\frac{BC}{2}=BM=CM.
\]
Thus the circle centered at \(M\) with radius \(BC/2\) passes through all three vertices. It is the circumcircle, so its center is the midpoint of the hypotenuse, choice C.
methods.levelReason: Uses the Grade 8 median-to-the-hypotenuse theorem and the basic definition of a circle, providing a lower-prerequisite geometric route.
